jobs.description:
About Blueprint

Blueprint is a technology solutions firm headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with teams across the United States. We help organizations turn complex challenges into meaningful outcomes by connecting strategy and execution across AI, cloud, data, product development, and emerging technology.

Our culture is built by people who care deeply about doing exceptional work. We set high standards, take ownership, and continually challenge ourselves and one another to be better. We work hard, support each other, and take genuine pride in what we deliver for our clients, partners, and teams.

At Blueprint, you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.

Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.

About the Role

We’re looking for an AI Response Labeler / Annotator with deep expertise in Korean and the cultural context of Korea.

This is an AI annotation and evaluation role, not a translation or traditional localization position. Korean expertise is an essential specialization, but it represents only one component of the work. You’ll evaluate AI-generated responses across a broad range of topics, tasks, and real-world scenarios. Much of the content, annotation guidance, and day-to-day work will be in English.

You’ll perform side-by-side comparisons of responses generated by different AI models and determine which response better meets the user’s needs. This requires strong analytical judgment, the ability to interpret detailed guidelines, and the consistency to apply those standards across a high volume of evaluations.

Successful candidates will be comfortable assessing content beyond language quality alone. You may be asked to evaluate factual accuracy, relevance, completeness, reasoning, instruction-following, clarity, safety, tone, and overall usefulness.

What You'll Do

  • Perform side-by-side comparisons of AI-generated responses and determine which response is stronger.
  • Evaluate responses for factual accuracy, relevance, completeness, clarity, reasoning, instruction-following, tone, and overall quality.
  • Assess content written in English, Korean, or a combination of both, depending on the assigned scenario.
  • Evaluate a broad range of content, including general-purpose questions and answers, web-search results, file-based tasks, image-based responses, content-generation requests, and single-turn and multi-turn conversations.
  • Apply Korean expertise when evaluating language, terminology, tone, regional conventions, idioms, and cultural context specific to Korea.
  • Evaluate the complete quality of a response rather than focusing only on grammar, translation, or language fluency.
  • Identify subtle but meaningful differences between responses, including unsupported claims, incomplete reasoning, missed instructions, unnatural phrasing, cultural inaccuracies, and differences in usefulness.
  • Apply detailed, scenario-specific annotation guidelines accurately and consistently.
  • Make independent evaluation decisions when examples or guidelines don’t provide an obvious answer.
  • Document decisions clearly and provide concise, evidence-based rationale when required.
  • Complete evaluations within established time and productivity expectations without sacrificing accuracy.
  • Maintain consistent judgment across a high volume of varied assignments.
  • Participate in training, guided practice, calibration sessions, qualification reviews, and ongoing quality-review activities.
  • Incorporate feedback and adjust evaluation decisions to remain aligned with team and client quality standards.

What You'll Bring

  • Native-level or professional fluency in Korean.
  • Deep familiarity with the linguistic conventions, regional vocabulary, idioms, tone, and cultural context of Korean as used in Korea.
  • Strong English fluency and reading comprehension, including the ability to understand complex prompts, AI-generated responses, and detailed annotation guidelines written in English.
  • Strong general analytical and critical-thinking skills that extend beyond language evaluation.
  • Ability to evaluate content across varied topics, formats, and task types.
  • Ability to assess factuality, relevance, reasoning, clarity, instruction-following, cultural appropriateness, and overall usefulness.
  • Ability to recognize subtle differences in meaning, quality, tone, and user intent.
  • Sound judgment when applying structured evaluation criteria to ambiguous or unfamiliar scenarios.
  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to explain evaluation decisions clearly and concisely.
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy while working within established time expectations.
  • Ability to learn and consistently apply detailed evaluation frameworks.
  • Ability to work independently while remaining aligned with shared quality standards.
  • Comfort performing repetitive, detail-oriented work for extended periods while maintaining focus, accuracy and consistent judgement.
  • Ability to receive feedback, recalibrate decisions, and adapt as evaluation guidelines evolve.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience performing side-by-side labeling, annotation, comparative content evaluation, or quality assessment.
  • Experience evaluating AI-generated responses or contributing to model-quality assessment.
  • Experience with data labeling or annotation.
  • Experience evaluating search relevance, content quality, factual accuracy, or user-facing digital experiences.
  • Experience working with detailed guidelines, rubrics, or structured decision-making frameworks.

Work Pace and Productivity Expectations

This is a highly structured and repetitive role that involves completing similar evaluation tasks throughout the workday. Candidates should be comfortable maintaining focus, accuracy, and consistent judgment while reviewing a high volume of AI-generated content.

Most evaluation tasks are expected to take approximately 15 minutes, and employees are generally expected to complete a minimum of 25 tasks per day. Some tasks may take more or less time depending on their complexity.

Success in this role requires balancing productivity with quality. Employees must meet established daily expectations while carefully applying annotation guidelines and providing accurate, well-supported evaluation decisions.

Training and Qualification

All new hires must successfully complete a structured onboarding and qualification program before beginning production work.

The program includes training sessions, guided practice exercises, calibration against established quality benchmarks, and a formal qualification review.

Training is intended to establish consistent evaluation judgment across the team. Language fluency alone will not be sufficient to qualify. Employees must also demonstrate the ability to evaluate broader response quality, follow detailed annotation guidelines, explain their decisions, and complete work within the expected timeframe.

Employees will continue to receive feedback, quality reviews, and calibration support after entering production.

Compensation

At Blueprint, we strive to offer competitive pay that reflects the value of our team members. Compensation for this role is influenced by a variety of factors, including skills, education, responsibilities, experience, and geographic market.

The anticipated compensation range is $38.46 to $40.87 USD per hour, with a midpoint of $39.66 USD per hour. Please note that we typically do not hire new employees at the top of the posted range. Actual starting pay will be determined based on experience, skills, and internal equity. The final compensation and job title may vary depending on the selected candidate’s qualifications.

Location and Work Arrangement

Remote within the United States.

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and reside within a U.S. time zone.

During the approximately 30-day training and qualification period, employees must work from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time. After successfully completing training, employees may work standard business hours within their local time zone.

Benefits

Blueprint believes that healthy, supported employees do their best work. Eligible employees have access to a comprehensive benefits package that may include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Competitive paid time off
  • Parental leave
  • Professional growth and development opportunities

Benefits and eligibility may vary based on role, employment status, and location.

That afternoon you are putting together an FMLA designation notice, then jumping on a call to walk a client's payroll administrator through a deduction correction. Next week you are deep in a new HRIS implementation, cleaning up employee data and testing the first payroll run.

If that variety sounds energizing rather than scattered, keep reading. If your instinct is that this work should be handed to someone else, this is not the right fit — and we would rather both of us know that now.
This is a permanent part-time, fully remote position. We are looking for someone who wants RCR to be their work — not a side engagement alongside other employment or their own consulting practice.

The Schedule

Core hours are 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Eastern, when we need you reachable for clients. The remaining hours each week are yours to place — early mornings, evenings, whatever fits your life. We hold this schedule seriously; it is the reason the role exists as part-time rather than full-time.

We do ask for flexibility to pick up additional hours occasionally when client needs spike — open enrollment, an implementation go-live, an urgent employee relations matter.

A Note on Career Breaks

We welcome applicants returning to the workforce after time away. A gap on your resume is not a mark against you here — we care that you have the experience and that you are ready to use it. If you stepped back from a career in HR and want back in, we would like to hear from you.

What You Will Actually Do

We wrote this section deliberately specific, because we want you to know exactly what you are signing up for.

Day-to-day HR execution — you do the work, not delegate it

  • Draft and send offer letters, and manage onboarding paperwork, I-9s, and background checks end to end
  • Prepare FMLA, ADA, and state leave notices and correspondence, and track leave cases from first request through return to work
  • Process and audit payroll: entering changes, chasing down discrepancies, reconciling deductions, resolving the check that came out $46 short
  • Maintain accurate employee data across HRIS platforms — you are the one in the system, not the one reviewing a report about the system
  • Build and update handbooks, policies, job descriptions, offer templates, and employee communications
  • Run open enrollment logistics: employee meetings, election tracking, carrier file follow-up, post-enrollment audits

Client service that earns the "wow"

  • Serve as the primary day-to-day HR contact for your clients — the person they call when something goes sideways
  • Respond fast, follow through completely, and close the loop without being asked twice
  • Handle a client's employee question with the same care whether it is a routine PTO balance or a resignation letter that just landed
  • Anticipate what is coming — the I-9 that expires next month, the notice that is due, the manager who will need coaching before that conversation

Projects and systems implementations

  • Work implementations start to finish: data gathering and cleanup, configuration testing, parallel payroll runs, employee communications, go-live support
  • Manage several client projects at once and keep every one of them moving
  • Document processes so the next person can run them

Employee relations and manager support

  • Investigate and resolve employee relations matters — complaints, performance concerns, policy violations — with discretion and clean documentation
  • Coach frontline and mid-level managers through performance conversations, write-ups, and terminations
  • Keep clients compliant with federal and state employment law: FMLA, ADA, FLSA, ACA, and the multi-state patchwork that comes with our client base

Who Thrives Here

  • You would rather have twelve things on your plate than three, and you have a system for keeping all of them straight
  • You get bored when work gets repetitive, and you look for the next problem to solve
  • You take real pride in being the person a client can count on — responsiveness is part of your professional identity, not a requirement someone imposed on you
  • You are comfortable being the one who does the task, files the form, fixes the record, and sends the email
  • You are steady when three clients need you at once and one of them is upset
  • You are detail-obsessed. A wrong date on a leave notice or a typo in an offer letter bothers you

Who This Is Not For

We say this plainly because false starts are expensive for everyone:
  • You are looking for advisory-only or strategy-only work. Roughly 70% of this job is execution. If you want to build the framework and hand it off, this will frustrate you.
  • You want to lead a team. There is no team to lead. You are an individual contributor, and you will stay one.
  • You are building or maintaining your own consulting practice. We are hiring an employee, not contracting a firm. This needs to be your primary professional commitment.
  • You want this as a second job. We are not a fit alongside other employment.
  • Administrative work feels beneath your level. Some days it is data entry and chasing signatures. If that reads as a step down, we are not the right place.
  • You need a lot of structure and ramp time. You will be supporting live clients within your first few weeks.

What You Bring

  • 7-10 years of hands-on HR generalist experience — and you are still doing the work yourself today, not overseeing others who do it
  • Real depth across the full HR lifecycle: recruiting and onboarding, payroll, benefits administration, leave administration, employee relations, and policy work
  • Payroll fluency. You have processed it, audited it, and fixed it — not just approved it.
  • Leave administration experience. You can produce a compliant FMLA notice without a template hunt.
  • HRIS proficiency and real experience with at least one implementation or platform migration
  • Strong writing. You can produce a polished handbook, a clear policy, and a professional employee email without heavy editing.
  • Working knowledge of federal and multi-state employment law, and good instincts about when to escalate
  • Proven remote work experience — you are self-directed, communicative, and reliably reachable during core hours
  • BA/BS in Human Resources or a related field

Preferred

  • Prior HR consulting, PEO, HRO, or multi-client experience
  • Experience supporting multiple entities or client organizations at once
  • PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP, or SHRM-SCP certification
  • Proficiency across the Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel

Compensation and Benefits

  • $32.00 - $05.00 per hour, depending on experience
  • Paid time off and paid holidays — uncommon in part-time HR work, and intentional on our part
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Professional development assistance, including certification support
  • Fully remote, with a consistent Monday-Friday schedule
We are hiring an employee, not contracting a firm. The benefits package reflects that.

We are committed to being an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.excerpt: About R77 GlobalR77 Global is a talent advisory partner connecting high-calibre professionals with ambitious organisations across iGaming, fintech, payments, financial services, technology and Web3.
jobs.description:
About R77 Global

R77 Global is a talent advisory partner connecting high-calibre professionals with ambitious organisations across iGaming, fintech, payments, financial services, technology and Web3. We represent opportunities with discretion and give candidates a clear, honest view of the role, its expectations and the environment they would be joining.

The opportunity

R77 Global is supporting our client in appointing a hands-on Head of Development to lead the technical direction, reliability and continued evolution of a complex financial technology platform.

The platform supports banking, payments, investment services, order management and in-house matching capabilities, alongside modern ML and LLM infrastructure. This is a senior technical leadership role for someone who is comfortable working close to money movement, transaction integrity and production systems where correctness is essential.

You will combine engineering leadership with hands-on systems thinking: guiding the team, shaping technical standards, challenging architecture and taking ownership when production behaviour does not match expectations. This is not a front-end leadership post or a ticket-management role.

The role

The Head of Development will have meaningful influence over engineering standards, platform resilience, technical risk and the future growth of the development function. The successful person will be expected to understand the running system, make evidence-led decisions and ensure changes protect the integrity of the wider financial platform.

R77 Global Head of Development

R77 GLOBAL | OPPORTUNITY BRIEF

Key responsibilities

Technical leadership and direction

  • Own the technical direction and engineering standards across the core platform.
  • Provide hands-on guidance, mentoring and constructive challenge to engineers working across multiple services and repositories.
  • Review architectural decisions and production changes affecting financial integrity, system performance, resilience and recovery.
  • Translate business priorities into a practical technical roadmap, balancing platform development with reliability and risk reduction.

Platform reliability and production ownership

  • Lead the investigation and resolution of complex production incidents across ledger, order-management, matching, payment and supporting services.
  • Trace transactions and failures across process boundaries, using logs, traces, data and network evidence to confirm the real cause.
  • Improve observability, incident response, recovery procedures and post-incident learning.
  • Define clear operational controls for stateful services and systems where a restart, retry or deployment could affect financial or order integrity.
  • Champion small, measured and targeted fixes rather than unnecessary architectural change.

Core financial and distributed systems

  • Protect the reliability and integrity of the platform's ledger, order-management and matching capabilities.
  • Guide technical decisions involving concurrency, binary protocols, clustered services, deterministic processing, replay and recovery.
  • Ensure the engineering team understands the operational difference between stateless applications and stateful financial systems.
  • Work confidently across Linux, Kubernetes and event-driven infrastructure, including the safe operation of stateful workloads.

Team and stakeholder leadership

  • Develop engineering capability through mentoring, code and design reviews, clear expectations and disciplined technical discussion.
  • Work closely with executive leadership, product, operations and security to communicate technical risk and agree priorities.
  • Support the continued growth of the development function, including future hiring and the evolution of team structure.

What we are looking for

Essential experience

  • Substantial commercial experience with C and/or C++ in production environments where memory layout, object lifetime, concurrency and failure behaviour are explicit.
  • Experience building, operating or diagnosing complex, high-performance or distributed systems.
  • The ability and willingness to work extensively with modern Java services and low-latency messaging technologies.
  • Strong Linux/Unix knowledge and proven production Kubernetes experience, including an understanding of stateful and stateless workloads.
  • The ability to follow a request, event or transaction across multiple services, protocols and repositories.
  • A strong record of diagnosing difficult production issues through measurable evidence rather than assumptions.
  • Experience leading technical decisions, mentoring engineers and raising development standards.
  • Clear, precise written and spoken English, particularly when communicating incidents, risk and technical decisions.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Experience in one or more of the following areas would be highly advantageous:
  • Matching engines, central limit order books, trading venues, exchange infrastructure or HFT.
  • Financial ledgers, payment platforms, settlement, order-management systems or transaction-processing environments.
  • Consensus protocols and low-latency messaging, including technologies such as Raft, Aeron, SBE, FIX or ISO 20022.
  • Java, TypeScript/Node.js, Postgres projectors and event-driven read models.
  • OpenTelemetry, structured logging and production observability.
  • Deterministic numerical or ML pipelines and production LLM inference environments.
  • Secure tool-calling, workload isolation, GPU capacity management or sandboxed execution.

What success will look like

Within the first 6-12 months, the successful person will be expected to have:

  • Established clear technical ownership and consistent engineering standards across the platform.
  • Improved incident investigation, observability and recovery readiness.
  • Strengthened the reliability of the core financial, order-management and matching systems.
  • Reduced operational risk around stateful deployments and high-impact platform changes.
  • Developed stronger technical capability and accountability across the engineering team.
  • Created a practical roadmap that balances resilience, platform evolution and commercial priorities.

Selection approach

The selection process will focus on real systems reasoning and production experience rather than framework lists or theoretical exercises. Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss:

A complex production incident they personally diagnosed and the evidence that identified the cause.

Memory, concurrency, distributed failure, replay and recovery scenarios.

The safe operation of stateful workloads within Kubernetes.

How they would distinguish between failures in a core system, a downstream projection, a gateway and a data-delivery path.

Salary and package

The anticipated base salary is €80,000-€120,000 gross annually, depending on experience. There may be flexibility for an exceptional candidate with highly relevant matching-engine, HFT, exchange-infrastructure or low-latency financial-systems expertise. The wider package and working arrangement will be discussed during the process.

How to apply

Please apply through R77 Global with a CV that clearly describes the production systems you have owned, together with a short note outlining one of the most difficult production issues you have diagnosed and the evidence that led you to the solution.

Candidates selected for an initial discussion will receive a more detailed technical brief covering the platform, responsibilities and selection process. All applications will be handled confidentially.

jobs.excerpt: This position is fully remote/home based.  Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK.
jobs.description:
This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK. This is a 12 month FTC.

Role Summary

PLOS is a nonprofit Open Access publisher with an ambitious mission: to help transform research communication so that science can be shared, understood and used more effectively. We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Product team for a 12-month maternity cover contract.It's an interesting time to join us.

Research publishing is changing rapidly. Researchers' expectations are changing. Technology is creating possibilities that didn't exist a few years ago. And at PLOS we're rethinking some of the services, systems and assumptions that have shaped scholarly publishing for decades.

That means there are interesting product problems to solve - not just features to deliver.

You'll take responsibility for a product area and work with designers, engineers and colleagues across PLOS to understand the problems that matter, work out where we can make the greatest difference and help the team learn its way towards good solutions.

Although this is a fixed-term role, it isn't a caretaker role. You'll be joining active product teams working on significant problems and will have plenty of opportunity to shape what we do and how we do it.

How we work

We want our product teams to be curious, evidence-led and comfortable with uncertainty.

We don't expect a Product Manager to arrive with all the answers. We do expect them to ask good questions.

You'll use continuous discovery alongside delivery: spending time with users, looking at data, understanding the wider service, identifying assumptions and finding practical ways to test them.

You'll help the team break large problems into smaller things we can learn from, rather than waiting until everything is known before we release something.

And you'll make the team's thinking visible - explaining what we're trying to achieve, what we've learned, what we're uncertain about and why we're making the choices we are.

Responsibilities

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll:

  • Understand the problem. Build a deep understanding of our users, their needs and behaviours, as well as the organisational, operational and technical context surrounding them.
  • Shape product direction. Work out where the greatest opportunities lie within your area and help translate PLOS's objectives into clear product outcomes and priorities.
  • Practise continuous discovery. Work closely with design, engineering and others to explore problems, identify assumptions and regularly test ideas with users and through data.
  • Turn uncertainty into learning. Frame hypotheses, design useful experiments and look for the smallest sensible way to learn whether we're heading in the right direction.
  • Make good product decisions. Weigh evidence, impact, effort, risk and opportunity when deciding what to pursue - and what not to pursue.
  • Measure whether things are getting better. Define useful measures of success and use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand whether our work is having the intended effect.
  • Work iteratively. Help the team deliver in small steps, learn from what happens and adapt rather than treating plans as fixed commitments.
  • Communicate your thinking. Clearly explain problems, evidence, choices, trade-offs and learning to people with very different levels of technical and product knowledge.
  • Create strong feedback loops. Use conversations, demos, reviews and other forums to get useful feedback early rather than presenting finished thinking late.
  • Work as part of a team. Create the conditions in which designers, engineers and other specialists can contribute to product decisions rather than treating product management as something the PM does alone.
  • Look beyond the product interface. Understand the wider service, including processes, systems and teams around it, and recognise when solving a user problem requires changing more than software.

Experience and qualifications

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification or equivalent professional experience. 
  • At least three years' experience working as a Product Manager in a multidisciplinary digital product team, working closely with disciplines such as design, engineering, research and delivery.
  • Experience using product discovery alongside delivery - for example, user research, data, experimentation and hypothesis testing - to understand problems and inform what a team should do next.
  • Experience working with significant uncertainty or ambiguity: identifying what is known, what is assumed and what needs to be learned before making larger commitments.
  • Experience taking complex problems and helping a team turn them into clear priorities, outcomes and practical next steps.
  • Experience making product decisions using a combination of user evidence, data, organisational goals, technical constraints and product judgement.
  • Experience communicating product thinking clearly to a wide range of people, including explaining evidence, uncertainty, trade-offs and why particular decisions have been made.
  • Experience working collaboratively with people outside the immediate product team, particularly where different groups have different needs, incentives or perspectives.

Particularly useful

We'd be especially interested in candidates who have experience of one or more of the following:

  • Working in an organisation going through significant product, digital or organisational transformation.
  • Working in complex service environments where improving the user experience involves changes to technology, operations, policy or organisational processes - not simply changing an interface.
  • Helping teams move towards more iterative, outcome-focused or evidence-led ways of working.
  • Working in a mission-led, research, publishing, education, scientific or other knowledge-based organisation.

Experience of scholarly publishing is useful but isn't required.

What we're looking for in a Senior Product Manager

For us, seniority isn't about having a larger backlog or knowing more product framework: it's about judgement.

You'll be able to take a complex and uncertain problem, help people understand it, decide what we most need to learn, bring a team together around a sensible course of action and change that course when the evidence tells us to.

You'll be comfortable making decisions without perfect information while being clear about the assumptions and risks involved.

And you'll help the people around you think more clearly about the product - not simply tell them what to build.

Working at PLOS

You'll join PLOS's Product team and work collaboratively with colleagues across Digital and the wider organisation.

The role has no direct line-management responsibility.

The job is fully remote. Some flexibility to work across time zones and occasional national or international travel may be required.

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is (UK) £65,000 - £75,500. PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below.

BENEFITS:

  • Private medical insurance
  • Life assurance
  • Income protection 
  • Personal accident insurance
  • Pension with up to 10% employer match
  • 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out.

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all.

Visit to learn more.

To learn more about how PLOS protects your privacy, see our Employee Privacy Notice.

jobs.excerpt: We are hiring a Software Engineer in the Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning job family to join our Enterprise AI Platform team in Israel.
jobs.description:
We are hiring a Software Engineer in the Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning job family to join our Enterprise AI Platform team in Israel.

The platform powers AI-assisted engineering workflows across Sandisk and is built on a hybrid on-prem and cloud architecture with agentic orchestration, an MCP ecosystem, an LLM gateway, and memory and knowledge layers. This role focuses on the AI harness: the platform's agentic command-line tooling and the framework of skills, tools, memory, and guardrails that turn a general-purpose model into a governed engineering agent.

As part of the role, you will build distributed software systems and apply them to the runtime, integrations, and evaluation loops that make AI agents reliable inside Sandisk's engineering environment. You will work closely with platform engineers in the US and India and with the firmware, validation, and lab teams in Israel who use the harness every day.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:
Harness Development: Build and extend the platform's agentic harness, including the CLI runtime, the framework of skills and tool definitions, context and memory management, sandboxing, and execution hooks that govern what an agent is allowed to do.

Distributed Systems: Design and implement the services behind the harness: gateway integrations, session and state management, job execution, caching, and the secure paths that connect developer machines to on-prem platform services.

AI Ecosystem Contribution: Develop MCP servers, skills, and integrations that expose engineering data and tools (Jira, test management, lab benches, internal systems) to agents in a governed way. Contribute reusable components back to the shared platform framework.

Applied AI Understanding: Use working knowledge of how LLM-based systems behave in practice, including tool calling, context windows, prompt and skill design, token cost, failure modes, and evaluation, to make agent workflows predictable and cost-aware.

Reliability & Observability: Instrument harness components with tracing, metrics, and evaluation pipelines. Debug agent behavior end-to-end across the CLI, gateway, and model layers. Participate in incident response and postmortems.

Engineering Quality: Write well-tested, maintainable code. Build automated tests and evaluation suites for agent behavior. Take part in code and design reviews.

Local Partnership: Act as the platform's engineering presence in Israel. Gather requirements from teams adopting the harness, support early users, and feed learnings back into the roadmap.

Continuous Learning: Track advances in agent frameworks, coding agents, MCP, and AI infrastructure, and bring practical improvements into the harness.

Required:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

2 to 3 years of professional software engineering experience building and operating backend or distributed systems in production.

Strong proficiency in Python; working knowledge of TypeScript/JavaScript. Hands-on experience designing services, REST or GraphQL APIs, asynchronous and event-driven systems, and reliable client-server communication.

Practical understanding of how modern AI systems work: LLM APIs, tool and function calling, context and memory management, RAG, embeddings, and evaluation. Able to explain why an agent failed, not only that it did.

Experience with, or demonstrated interest in, agentic frameworks and protocols such as LangGraph, LangChain, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Experience with Docker and containerized deployments; exposure to Kubernetes and hybrid on-prem and cloud environments.

Working knowledge of relational databases (PostgreSQL), in-memory stores (Redis / Valkey), and vector databases.

Familiarity with enterprise security and identity basics: OAuth, OIDC, SSO, and secrets handling.

Comfortable in Linux and terminal-centric development workflows, including Git and CI/CD.

Preferred:

jobs.description:
At Talkspace, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission of getting therapy in the hands of everyone!

We are looking for an experienced UX Designerto join our Product team. In this role, you will partner closely with Product Managers, Designers, and Engineering to design new features and funnels, as well as evolve existing customer-facing product lines across all platforms. You'll bring thoughtful, user-centered thinking to projects ranging from focused feature work to end-to-end flows, reporting into our Director of UX. To work at Talkspace, you need to be as passionate as we are about our work, and excited to partner with us on delivering quality mental healthcare.

This is a remote position based on Eastern Time. Talkspace Headquarters is located in NYC.

What You’ll Do

  • Design end-to-end user experiences across web, iOS, and Android — from early concept and user flows through wireframes, prototypes, and production-ready design files
  • Partner with Product Managers and Engineering to scope, design, and ship new features and funnels, as well as improvements to existing customer-facing product lines
  • Design and support conversion and growth experiments (e.g., onboarding, sign-up, and checkout flows) as well as features that drive engagement and retention and reduce churn
  • Create wireframes, interactive prototypes, and high-fidelity mockups in Figma, and maintain organized, up-to-date design files and documentation
  • Contribute to and help evolve Talkspace's design system, ensuring consistency and reusability across platforms
  • Support and help execute user research and usability testing; translate findings and data-driven insights into concrete design decisions
  • Apply accessibility and platform-specific best practices (iOS, Android, Web) to ensure designs are intuitive, inclusive, and technically feasible
  • Incorporate motion, audio, and animation thoughtfully where they improve the user experience
  • Present design rationale and recommendations clearly to cross-functional stakeholders, incorporating feedback and building consensus
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Data/Analytics, and Brand to ensure designs are aligned, technically sound, and on-brand
  • Stay current on UX, interaction design, and visual design trends, bringing fresh thinking to the team

About You

  • 4+ years of experience as a UX Designer creating digital-first products (iOS, Android, and web), ideally in mass-market digital consumer products/apps, subscription-based, or e-commerce. Prior experience with digital healthcare/behavioral health is a plus
  • Experience designing a variety of project types and features, including but not limited to: conversion and growth experiments, and consumer-focused features that drive engagement, retention, and reduce churn
  • Experience supporting or executing user research and usability testing, and translating findings into actionable design decisions
  • Solid understanding of iOS, Android, and Web standard UX/UI practices
  • Strong proficiency in Figma (Sketch a plus)

Benefits

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision plans
  • Pre-tax benefits: HSA/ FSA
  • 401k Retirement Savings Program with matching up to 4%
  • Voluntary benefits including disability, basic life or pet insurance, etc.
  • Monthly Wellness Stipend to promote mental and physical self-care
  • Flexible PTO and Remote First Environment
  • Regular team events, including Wellness Workshops and Team Building Events
  • Free access to Talkspace products for you and one household member, as well as access to a friends and family discount!

Compensation

At Talkspace, we believe that pay transparency during the interview process is a critical part of diversity, equity, and inclusion. Our salary bands are based on internal and external compensation benchmarks, which we regularly evaluate to ensure we pay competitively.

The base salary range for this role is between $100,000 - $150,000. Within the salary bands, leveling corresponds to each candidate’s relevant experience, skills as assessed during the interview process, education, and applicable certifications.

Why Talkspace?

Talkspace is the world’s leading online therapy company, serving over 2 million users looking to begin their wellness journey through tele-health. According to the World Health Organization, close to 1 billion people worldwide live with a mental disorder, and on average more than 75% with mental, neurological, and substance use disorders receive no treatment for their condition at all. Additionally, one-third of the world’s population – 2 billion people – live in countries that spend less than 1% of their health budgets on mental health. Therapy is an universal need and it's our mission here to change the world by cultivating an intentional space for people to feel supported through quality care that is simple and accessible.

Combining our passion for innovation along with our desire to help others overcome the stigma behind “getting help,” we are transforming the way patients find the right care provider, making an otherwise impossible feat easily conquerable. Our network of licensed, accredited, and board-certified clinicians are increasing access to mental health for our members through a myriad of high quality therapy services: anytime and for a fraction of the price. Dedicated to our mission, we are looking for candidates that want to bring their talents into a diverse “for purpose” space. If you’re equally as passionate about making quality mental healthcare accessible to all then Talkspace is the right place for you!

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team.

Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

Kruze Consulting provides accounting, bookkeeping, finance, payroll, and tax services to over 750 startups backed by top tier venture capital funds. The AccountingSales Executive is the first point of contact for prospective clients who have requested information about accounting, tax, and financial services for their venture-backed startup. You will conduct introductory calls and prepare service quotes based on each prospect’s current and projected needs as they grow.

This role is built for someone who understands accounting and finance and wants to put that knowledge to work in a client-facing, commercial role. If you have spent time in accounting, bookkeeping, tax, or an outsourced finance function, and you find you enjoy the client conversations more than the compliance deadlines, this is a way to use your expertise every day without month-end close or busy season. Your credibility with founders will come from genuinely knowing the work, not from a script.

The ideal candidate is a natural relationship builder, an excellent communicator, highly organized, and detail-oriented. Kruze Consulting has a proven track record of developing its people to their highest potential. If you want to grow in a consultative, revenue-facing role at an entrepreneurial, fully remote professional services
firm, this is a terrific opportunity to do it.
KRUZE CONSULTING IS AN EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.
Kruze Consulting believes in diversity of thought as a competitive advantage to bring people together to build a culturally inclusive team. If you are smart, and good at what you do, come as you are. Diverse candidates (however you choose or choose not to identify) are encouraged to apply.
WHAT WE OFFER/WHY KRUZE CONSULTING:
  • Fully Remote – We’ve completely embraced and invested in remote work and know the benefits. Save time, save money, and decrease stress. Our experience shows that remote work fosters a healthier work/life balance for our people. We do get together once a year for an annual offsite meeting, but in-person attendance is optional.
  • Flexibility/Autonomy - Need to run to an appointment, your child's school, or just want to take a walk outside? No problem. If your clients’ needs are met and your work gets done on time, enjoy!
  • Stability – While we serve startups, we aren’t one. We’ve been around for almost a decade enjoying controlled growth over that time. We don’t over-hire, and thankfully, we’ve never had to do a reduction in force. Our service offering is niche, accounting is essential to businesses, and the potential market for our services is diversified/vast.
  • High-Quality Colleagues - We’re a diverse bunch, experts in our respective fields, and eager to help each other and clients. We care about each other as whole human beings.
  • High-Quality Clients - We work exclusively with venture-funded technology startups and early-stage companies who are creating some of the most exciting and transformative products and services in the world! (We also have a “no jerks” policy; our clients treat our people professionally and respectfully.)
  • Purpose/Meaningful Work – This is not your average accounting role. Kruze professionals get to work with innovative startups that are disrupting their respective industries and creating the products and services of tomorrow. Like proud parents, we derive vicarious enjoyment as our clients grow, get additional rounds of funding, and ultimately get acquired by Fortune 500 firms.

  • Experience in a consulting or outsourced bookkeeping/accounting firm
  • Experience selling accounting or professional services to business leaders
  • Experience in an enterprise SaaS company
  • Experience with Salesforce or similar CRM
  • A general understanding of the corporate tax filing process
  • Experience working with early-stage VC-backed startups

Job Responsibilities
  • Review, evaluate, and adjudicate a high volume of daily commercial credit submissions, including financial statement analysis, collateral evaluation, and business history review
  • Recommend appropriate risk-based pricing and deal structure; direct, coordinate, and make recommendations for lease approvals
  • Conduct background investigation including bank, finance company, and trade references, and confirmation of revenue sources
  • Identify transactions to be funded via Beacon's portfolio or third-party funding partners, and manage a pipeline of “in credit” transactions in a timely manner
  • Assist in the underwriting of portfolio acquisitions and/or portfolio sales
  • Maintain working familiarity with Beacon's core industry assets and business borrowers
  • Manage and grow relationships with Beacon's syndicate bank and funding partners
  • Negotiate improved financing terms and conditions with syndication and funding partners
  • Identify and establish new syndication bank programs and funding partnerships
  • Assist in the development and ongoing enhancement of corporate credit scoring strategy and credit policy manual

Senior EA to act as Kelly's right hand across two growing businesses. High trust, high autonomy, real judgment required.

Harkened/Fibras Unidas is a B2B knitwear manufacturing operation in Lima, now largely managed by a general manager. The Endery is a clothing brand that started in e-commerce and has expanded into wholesale, and now includes a physical presence in both Lima and the US. The team includes full-time employees, contractors, and fractional specialists across both countries.

The businesses have grown organically, but the systems haven't always kept pace. Too much still funnels back to Kelly - information, follow-up, cross-functional coordination, and one-off decisions. This hire will help to reallocate some of the responsibilities, and will be a long-term right hand to Kelly - providing continuity as things evolve. The EA will deeply understand how Kelly works, know the team/who owns what, create structure where needed, route work effectively, and make sure tasks that have been delegated are completed. The EA will be trusted to operate independently - absorbing context, exercising judgment, turning messy inputs into organized action, and attempting to only bring Kelly in when absolutely necessary.

We're looking for a Senior Executive Assistant. Someone who has already had a senior career and now wants a high-trust, high-autonomy right-hand role rather than climbing a traditional corporate ladder. You'll act as the central nervous system across the 2 businesses and their founder’s day-to-day life - the person who makes everything run smoothly.

📋 Own founder’s inbox and calendar, triaging incoming requests and handling or routing as much as possible

🤝 Act as connective tissue across the businesses - understand who owns what, get the right people talking to each other, and land work with the most effective person

✅ Close loops by tracking requests, commitments and action items until they're completed

💡 Prepare decisions and meetings so I receive distilled information, recommendations and clearly defined choices rather than raw problems

📦 Build and maintain systems that make the businesses easier to run - Notion, SOPs, Google Drive, recurring calendars and checklists

📊 Maintain oversight of recurring administrative and business-critical areas like compliance deadlines, benefits, trademarks, expenses, subscriptions, travel and other operational details

🎯 Support cross-functional and special projects by coordinating internal team members, contractors and outside experts

🧠 Learn founder’s working style and the businesses deeply enough to increasingly anticipate needs and handle issues independently

Working hours are roughly 6am-2pm New York time (midday-8pm in Eastern Europe/South Africa).

Requirements

To be successful in this role, you need:

✅ Proper Senior EA experience - Senior EA, Executive Business Partner, Chief of Staff/EA hybrid, or similarly high-ownership executive support experience (not a low-level VA)

✅ Excellent judgment - able to distinguish what you can decide independently, what should be delegated to someone else, and what genuinely needs exec’s attention

✅ Confidence to step in and make decisions with the information you have and keep things moving forward

✅ Comfort operating with ambiguity - able to take a messy or incomplete request, figure out what's actually needed, and create a path forward

✅ Strong attention to detail

✅ Comfort managing people laterally - chasing and following up with the wider team

✅ Self-motivated, self-starter approach - highly autonomous and comfortable working independently without frequent check-ins or reassurance

✅ Emotional steadiness and resilience - able to receive direct feedback, navigate pressure and interpersonal complexity, and remain calm and solutions-oriented

✅ Solid working knowledge of platforms, tech and AI tools

Brownie points for:

⭐ Some Spanish, or interest in learning Spanish (part of my inbox is in Spanish and my team is in Peru)

The ideal person is warm, kind and polite, but with get-things-done energy. Someone who fits the culture of the existing team - people who care about what they do and how they treat each other. Confident without being arrogant. Low-drama and emotionally stable. Thrives on getting their head down and doing the work with minimal check-ins. Success looks like one-line weekly emails I can quickly answer, not play-by-play updates. Things get done without requiring my time.

jobs.excerpt: Location: Remote, United States.  Core availability 9:00 a.
jobs.description:
Location: Remote, United States. Core availability 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern, Monday through Friday.

Type: Full time, salaried.

Eligibility: U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident.

The role

This is the analytical center of the contract and the face of it to the client. When a comment period closes on a proposed Packers and Stockyards Act rule, you are the person who reads what the public sent in, works out what actually matters in it, and turns thousands of pages into something the agency's policy staff can use to write a final rule.

Between rulemakings you run the contract: the deliverable tracking, the monthly reporting, the weekly client meetings, and the readiness work that makes the next sprint survivable. You will also direct the analyst bench during comment closes, setting the coding scheme and reviewing what comes back.

The turnaround is fifteen calendar days from the close of the comment period for both the substantive analysis and the key issues matrix, and the client has signaled they may want it faster. This job suits someone who does careful work quickly and does not need to be managed through a deadline.

Analysis and writing

  • Analyze public comments submitted on proposed rules, identifying themes, high-risk issues, quantitative metrics such as comment counts by topic, recommendations from the public, and the line between substantive and non-substantive submissions.
  • Distinguish organized form-letter campaigns from unique substantive comments and account for both in the analysis.
  • Identify every issue raised through public comment and build the key issues matrix, with comments sorted and categorized by issue for policy discussion and for drafting written responses in the final rule.
  • Write summaries that hold up under legal and policy review and that support the agency's response obligations under the Administrative Procedure Act.
  • Deliver written material that meets federal, and preferably USDA, style guidance and Section 508 accessibility requirements.
  • Set the coding scheme for each rulemaking and review the analyst bench's output against it.

Running the contract

  • Maintain a one-page deliverable tracking sheet, updated weekly and submitted electronically to the client throughout the contract.
  • Lead the kick-off meeting within ten business days of award and develop the project plan that follows from it.
  • Write and submit monthly progress reports to the Contracting Officer's Representative covering technical progress, schedule status, and any concerns or recommendations.
  • Run weekly virtual status meetings with the client on comment volume, processing progress, schedule risk, and emerging themes, and document decisions in internal meeting notes.
  • Forecast comment volume as it accumulates and tell Connexus early how much bench support each close will need.
  • Escalate anything that looks like scope creep to Connexus management rather than absorbing it.

What you need

  • Bachelor's degree. Advanced degree in public policy, law, economics, agricultural economics, or a related field is welcome.
  • Thorough working understanding of the federal notice-and-comment rulemaking process and the Administrative Procedure Act.
  • Direct experience analyzing or responding to public comments on a federal rulemaking, whether at an agency, a contractor, a law firm, or a trade association.
  • Demonstrable knowledge of federal regulatory and stylistic requirements for public comment processing and rulemaking.
  • Strong analytical writing. You will be asked for a writing sample.
  • Familiarity with the Federal Document Management System and regulations.gov.
  • Experience producing Section 508 compliant documents.
  • Comfortable owning a client relationship, including writing status reports a federal reviewer will read closely.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Teams, Zoom, and Adobe Acrobat Pro.

Nice to have

  • USDA experience, particularly with AMS, or familiarity with the Packers and Stockyards Act and livestock and poultry markets.
  • Experience with high-volume comment dockets and mass-comment campaigns.
  • Prior work directing junior analysts on deadline.
  • Working knowledge of qualitative coding or text analysis tooling.
Salary: $95K+ DOE

Voor een strategisch digitaliseringsproject binnen een politionele context in Antwerpen zoeken we een Senior Full Stack Developer die meewerkt aan de verdere uitbouw van een modulair case-managementplatform.

Je komt terecht in een multidisciplinair Agile team waar samenwerking, kwaliteit en continue verbetering centraal staan. Het platform is opgebouwd volgens een microservices-architectuur en ondersteunt verschillende kernprocessen.

  • Je ontwikkelt applicaties en functionaliteiten end-to-end.
  • Je voert programmatieopdrachten zeer vlot uit: coderen, testen en debuggen.
  • Je draagt bij aan de verdere evolutie van het platform en aan de digitalisering van de werking.
  • Je neemt een trekkersrol op binnen het team en helpt mee de technische richting te bepalen.
  • Je begeleidt en coacht ontwikkelaars en neemt waar nodig een development lead-rol op.
  • Je werkt volgens Scrum en een Agile ontwikkelingsmethodiek, met aandacht voor kwaliteit en samenwerking.

📝 Jouw profiel

  • Je hebt aantoonbare senior ervaring in full stack development en in de ontwikkeling van applicaties.
  • Je beschikt over sterke kennis van JavaScript, React, NodeJs en CSS.
  • Je hebt ervaring met microservices, Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis en RabbitMG.
  • Je bent vertrouwd met Elixir en met toepassingen die grote datavolumes verwerken.
  • Je hebt ervaring als development lead, inclusief het leiden van een ontwikkelteam en het coachen van ontwikkelaars.
  • Je kan zelfstandig en zeer vlot coderen, testen en debuggen.
  • Je hebt aantoonbare kennis van Scrum-methodologie en van een Agile ontwikkelingsmethodiek waarin je ook een leidende rol kan opnemen.
  • Je hebt ervaring met AI Coding tools.
  • Je beheerst het Nederlands op Europees CEFR-niveau C2.

💼 Aanbod

Je zal deel uitmaken van een groeiende KMO met ruimte voor initiatief en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Wij zorgen ervoor dat je in een uitdagende maar aangename werkomgeving terecht komt met leuke collega's. Samen met jou stippelen we een carriereplan uit, met aandacht en budget voor bijkomende opleidingingen / certificaties. Je kan rekenen op een motiverend salaris, aangevuld met extralegale voordelen, inclusief bedrijfswagen (of alternatieve vergoeding).

(Freelance is ook mogelijk)

jobs.description:
Who we are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

About the role

We are seeking a highly skilled Lead Testing Tools Development Engineer to design, develop, and maintain advanced testing frameworks and automation tools. This role focuses on building scalable, reusable, and integrated testing infrastructure that supports functional, performance, and security testing across diverse platforms and environments.

.

What you’ll get to do

Tool Development & Framework Design:

  • Design & implement custom test automation frameworks for functional, performance, and security testing
  • Develop reusable libraries, plugins, and CLI tools to support test execution, reporting, and integration with CI/CD pipelines
  • Build scalable test harnesses for distributed systems, microservices, mobile native and cloud SaaS applications.

Automation & Scripting:

  • Write robust, maintainable code in Java, JavaScript/TypeScript to automate test workflows.
  • Integrate tools with version control systems (Git), CI/CD platforms (Jenkins, Harness), and artifact repositories

DevOps & Infrastructure Integration:

  • Containerize tools using Docker and orchestrate test environments using Kubernetes
  • Implement observability into test tools using New Relic, Grafana, ELK Stack

Collaboration & Enablement:

  • Partner with QE, SRE/DevOps, and development teams to understand testing pain points and deliver tooling solutions.
  • Provide governance model, documentation, training, and support to enable teams to adopt and extend testing tools effectively.

Innovation & Continuous Improvement:

  • Evaluate and adopt emerging technologies in the testing ecosystem.
  • Contribute to internal best practices for test automation, tool development, & quality engineering.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML-based test generation or test impact analysis.
  • Background in developer experience (DevEx) or internal platform engineering

To succeed in this role, we think you should have

  • 12+ years of experience in Quality Engineering and Tools development or similar role.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related engineering discipline.
  • Strong programming skills in Java with a focus on tooling and automation.
  • Proficiency in extending and customizing open-source tools such as.
    • Functional/UI Testing: Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, Appium
    • API Testing: Postman/Bruno, REST Assured, Karate
    • Performance Testing: JMeter, K6, Gatling, Locust
    • Security Testing: OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, Nmap, Nessus
  • Experience Integrating testing tools with
    • Test Management & Issue Tracking: Jira, Qmetry
    • Reporting & Analytics: ReportPortal, Allure, ExtentReports, Grafana
    • CI/CD Pipelines: Jenkins, Harness, ArgoCD, GitLab, SonarQube
    • Device Farms: BrowserStack, LambdaTest for cross-platform and mobile testing
  • Experience with test data management, mocking frameworks, and service virtualization tools such as WireMock, Hoverfly, or Mockito
  • Strong command of relational (SQL) and non-relational (NoSQL) databases, along with experience in publish-subscribe messaging systems like Kafka.
  • Solid understanding of RESTful APIs, gRPC, WebSockets, & event-driven or asynchronous architectures
  • Hands-on experience with leading cloud platforms - Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and expertise in Kubernetes for container orchestration.
  • Proficient in working within Linux/Unix-based environments, including shell scripting and system-level debugging.
  • Well-versed in Agile/Scrum/Kanban methodologies, with a focus on iterative development and continuous delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability in problem-solving, root cause analysis, and debugging complex systems across the stack.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a proven track record of working effectively in cross-functional teams.

What we can offer you

  • Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human.
  • Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks.
  • Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits.

What to expect in the hiring process

  • A preliminary call with the recruiter
  • A call with the Hiring Manager
  • A technical Interview with members of the Engineering Team
  • A technical Interview with a members of the QA Team
  • A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.
  • All Interview stages are Virtual

Moniepoint is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

jobs.title: QA Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About Halborn Inc Our mission is to provide value-add security services and products to the world’s most cutting edge technology firms and that starts with blockchain tech.
jobs.description:
About Halborn Inc

Our mission is to provide value-add security services and products to the world’s most cutting edge technology firms and that starts with blockchain tech. Founded in 2019, Halborn is an elite cyber security company focused on solving complex adversarial problems unique to the cryptocurrency and fintech industries. From breaches and social engineering to stolen private keys and economic hacks, Halborn solves it. Our clientele are the exclusive blockchain companies as well as new startups with high growth trajectories.

Our Culture

Halborn is a globally distributed team of 100+, looking to grow our elite team of white hat hackers, sales professionals, security engineers and DevSecOps specialists who value independence, want to make their own hours, work for themselves and have a passion for the ever evolving cryptocurrency industry.

Our Commitment to Diversity

Halborn Inc is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, education, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics and celebrates the diversity of its growing team.

We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment Visas at this time.

Recruitment agencies and consultants may not submit resumes/CVs through this website or directly to managers. Halborn does not accept unsolicited agency resumes, and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with Halborn Inc.

We are looking for a QA Engineer who treats manual testing as a temporary condition. You will own quality across the internal platforms our security researchers depend on and the client-facing products that deliver our findings — and you will build the automation, tooling, and AI-assisted workflows that make that coverage possible without a headcount-shaped bottleneck. If your instinct when you see a repetitive process is to write the thing that replaces it, you will fit here.

Responsibilities

  • Own the test strategy for Halborn's internal engineering platforms and client-facing products, from unit and integration coverage through end-to-end and regression suites.
  • Design, build and maintain automated test suites in code — UI, API, and data-layer — and keep them fast, deterministic, and trusted by the engineers who depend on them.
  • Use LLM-assisted tooling to accelerate test authoring, generate edge cases from specs and diffs, triage failing runs, and summarize regressions for the team.
  • Build and tune quality gates in CI/CD so that broken builds never reach a client environment, and so that the feedback loop stays measured in minutes.
  • Identify manual QA processes and automate them out of existence — release checklists, environment setup, test data generation, smoke verification, reporting.
  • Reproduce, isolate, and file defects with unambiguous repro steps, expected versus actual behavior, and enough context for an engineer to fix it without a follow-up conversation.
  • Partner with security engineers to fold security regression checks — authentication, authorization, input handling, secrets exposure — into the standard pipeline.
  • Run performance, load, and reliability testing against services handling sensitive audit and engagement data.
  • Define and report the quality metrics that matter: escaped defect rate, flake rate, coverage of critical paths, and time to detection.
  • Contribute to release readiness decisions and act as an informed voice on whether something ships.

Qualifications

  • 3 to 5 years in QA engineering, SDET, or test automation, with a demonstrated shift from manual execution toward automated coverage.
  • Strong programming ability in at least one of TypeScript, JavaScript, or Python — you write test code that other engineers are willing to read and maintain.
  • Hands-on experience with modern automation frameworks such as Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, pytest, or equivalent.
  • Practical API testing experience, including contract, integration, and negative-path testing against REST or GraphQL services.
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar) and comfort owning pipeline configuration yourself.
  • Daily, deliberate use of AI coding assistants and LLM tooling in your own workflow, with a clear point of view on where they help and where they must be verified.
  • Comfort with Git, containerized local environments, and reading application code to understand what you are testing rather than testing blind.
  • Excellent written communication — in a distributed, asynchronous team, a well-written bug report or test plan is the deliverable.
  • High autonomy and strong self-direction in a fast-moving environment where priorities shift.
  • Willingness to learn the technical aspects of blockchain, smart contracts, and cybersecurity.

Bonus Points

  • Experience testing Web3 applications — wallet flows, testnets, RPC interactions, or smart contract tooling such as Foundry or Hardhat.
  • Experience building evaluation harnesses for LLM-powered features, including regression testing of non-deterministic output.
  • Background in security testing, OWASP methodology, or hands-on time with tools like Burp Suite.
  • Performance and load testing with k6, Locust, JMeter, or similar.
  • Experience with observability tooling and using production telemetry to find gaps in test coverage.
  • Open source contributions to testing frameworks or developer tooling.
  • Knowledgeable of the latest trends in Blockchain and DeFi.

jobs.excerpt: Our client, a leading Software, Information and Communication Technologies company, operates internationally (Athens, Brussels, Luxembourg, Copenhagen, Stockholm, London, Nicosia, Hong-Kong, Valetta, etc).
jobs.description:
Our client, a leading Software, Information and Communication Technologies company, operates internationally (Athens, Brussels, Luxembourg, Copenhagen, Stockholm, London, Nicosia, Hong-Kong, Valetta, etc). Our client is a renowned supplier of IT services to government institutions, multinational corporations, public administrations and multinational companies, research and academic institutes.

Role Overview

Our client currently has a vacancy for a Scrum Master to offer his/her services as an expert remotely within the EU. In the context of the first assignment, the successful candidate will be integrated in the team of the company that will closely cooperate with a major client’s IT team on site.

Job Type: B2B Contract

Workplace: Remote

Requirements

  • University Degree and at least 8 years of IT professional experience;
  • Minimum of 3 of dedicated experience working as a Scrum Master at SM2 level or above;
  • Led at least 2 production teams through full sprint cycles (planning, review, retrospective, and refinement);
  • Implemented data-driven continuous improvement initiatives, such as increasing team velocity or reducing lead time;
  • Experience coordinating cross-team work via Scrum-of-Scrums or PI Planning events;
  • Deep knowledge of the Scrum Guide and Agile Manifesto principles and values;
  • Good knowledge of facilitation techniques (e.g., Fist of Five, participatory decision-making, Liberating Structures);
  • Good knowledge of systems-thinking and process tailoring to fit complex or evolving environments;
  • Good knowledge of team motivation and stakeholder engagement techniques (e.g., information radiators, team empowerment models);
  • Good knowledge of Agile metrics (velocity, cycle time, burn-up/down charts, cumulative flow diagrams) and the ability to build and interpret dashboards to support team performance and forecasting;
  • Tool proficiency in Azure DevOps (preferred) or Jira, particularly in backlog management, dashboards, and workflow configuration;
  • Possession of Scrum Master certifications: PSM II (or higher) and SAFe 5/6 Agilist;
  • Experience with one or more scaled Agile frameworks (SAFe, Nexus, LeSS, etc.) is considered as an asset;
  • Knowledge of integrating SAFe and Kanban approaches to optimize flow and delivery predictability is considered as an asset;
  • Excellent command of the English language.

Responsibilities

  • Organize and facilitate agile activities and ceremonies including daily stand-up meetings, sprint reviews, retrospectives, sprint and release planning, and product backlog refinement sessions;
  • Ensure that all meetings are positive, productive, stay on topic, and are kept within the timebox;
  • Collaborate closely with the product owner to manage the backlog;
  • Coach team and Product Owner on empiricism, value‑based backlog slicing, and incremental delivery;
  • Track and radiate flow metrics (velocity, sprint burndown, iteration burn rate) and guide the team in data‑driven improvement;
  • Champion and facilitate adoption of agile standards, tools, and best practices;
  • Proactively identify and resolve impediments to team progress;
  • Promote empowered, self‑organising teams, shared vision, psychological safety, collaborative decisions (e.g., Fist‑of‑Five);
  • Uphold Definition of Done, quality gates, and compliance with organisational standards;
  • Communicate with other SCRUM masters and product owners across the organization to ensure transparency into delivery progress, challenges, and risks;
  • Utilize team feedback and metrics (e.g., quality, delivery, cadence, etc.) to identify areas of opportunity and work with team to continuously improve;
  • Support the team in using agile planning and development tools (e.g. Azure DevOps, Confluence);
  • Experiment with new practices and frameworks to improve team outcomes;
  • Actively participate in learning opportunities such as communities of practice or conferences to improve skills and better support the team;
  • Contribute to the advancement and improvement of agile practices within the organization.
